```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r load-model}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Solms_2019_rivaroxaban"))
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12444> (PMC6875705, open access)

Solms 2019 links rivaroxaban plasma concentration to prothrombin time (PT)
so that the PT measured in large phase III trials, where few or no PK samples
were taken, could sharpen the individual exposure estimates used in the
exposure-response analyses the EMA requested. The packaged model is the
**population PK/PT model** of the paper:

* the PK layer is the integrated popPK model of Willmann 2018a (packaged
  separately as `Willmann_2018a_rivaroxaban`), with every PK parameter fixed
  to its final estimate, and
* PT rises linearly with the individual predicted concentration,
  `PT = BASE + SLOPE * Cc`, with exponential interindividual variability on
  BASE and SLOPE and a proportional residual error.

Three source documents were used:

* the main article (Tables 1-3, Results);
* Supplementary Figure S2, whose legend writes out the PK/PT model and gives
  the final estimates with their RSEs, **including the PT residual error
  (CV 11.4%)** that the main text does not print; and
* the Supplementary Model Code, which holds the NONMEM control streams of the
  integrated popPK model, the popPK/PT model, the "eta approach" and the R code
  of the "PT covariate approach". The popPK/PT control stream fixes the PK
  parameters to the Willmann 2018a final estimates at more digits than that
  paper prints, and those values are used here. Its `$THETA` values for BASE
  and SLOPE (12 and 0.04) and `$OMEGA` values for their IIV (0.3) are initial
  estimates; the final estimates come from the Results and Figure S2.

The PT-adjustment *regression functions* of Table 2 are not a simulation
model -- they map a per-patient summary of observed PT onto a correction
factor for an already-computed exposure. They are reproduced below as a
post-processing step on the simulated output rather than packaged in
`model()`.

No erratum or corrigendum was found for this article (Crossref `relation` /
`update-to` metadata and the JATS record were checked on 2026-11-26).

# Population

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

The PK/PT model was fitted to 1,779 patients with time-matched PK and PT
samples (Table 1): 508 from ODIXa-HIP2 and 322 from ODIXa-KNEE (VTE prevention
after hip or knee replacement), 437 from ODIXa-DVT and 351 from the
EINSTEIN-DVT dose-ranging study (VTE treatment), and 161 from the ROCKET AF PK
substudy (atrial fibrillation). PT was measured centrally with a
rivaroxaban-sensitive thromboplastin (STA Neoplastine / Neoplastine CI Plus).
The paper does not tabulate the demographics of this PK-PT data set.

# Deterministic gates

## The PK layer is the Willmann 2018a model

The popPK/PT control stream fixes the PK parameters to the Willmann 2018a
final estimates. Solving both packaged models for the same typical patient
must give the same concentrations up to the rounding of the three-significant-
figure values printed in Willmann 2018a Table 3.

```{r pk-layer-gate}
ref_cov <- data.frame(
  CRCL = 93, BSA = 1.92, WT = 81, AGE = 61, SEXF = 0,
  CONMED_PGP_INH = 0, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_STRONG = 0,
  CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_MOD = 0, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_WEAK = 0,
  CONMED_CYP3A4_IND = 0, DIS_AF = 0, DIS_ACS = 0, DIS_VTE_P = 0
)

# Event table for one subject: `dose_mg` every `tau` h for `n_dose` doses,
# observed on `obs_times` on the central compartment. dvid = 1 on observation
# rows is needed because the model declares two endpoints (Cc and PT); every
# endpoint column is still returned.
make_events <- function(id, dose_mg, tau, n_dose, obs_times, cov) {
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau, evid = 1L,
    amt = dose_mg, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_,
    cmt = "central", dvid = 1L
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(DOSE_RIVAROXABAN_MG = dose_mg) |>
    dplyr::cross_join(cov) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_ref <- make_events(1L, 20, 24, 10, seq(216, 240, by = 0.5), ref_cov)

sim_solms <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui, ev_ref,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
)
sim_willmann <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Willmann_2018a_rivaroxaban")),
  dplyr::select(ev_ref, -dvid),
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame"
)
rel_diff <- abs(sim_solms$Cc - sim_willmann$Cc) / sim_willmann$Cc
max(rel_diff)
stopifnot(nrow(sim_solms) == nrow(sim_willmann), max(rel_diff) < 0.01)
```

## The PT equation

```{r pt-equation-gate}
# PT is the error-free linear transform of the error-free concentration; with
# no random effects BASE = 13.1 s and SLOPE = 0.031 s per ug/L exactly.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(sim_solms$PT - (13.1 + 0.031 * sim_solms$Cc))) < 1e-8
)
range(sim_solms$PT)
```

At the typical reference patient on 20 mg once daily the steady-state PT
swings between about `r round(min(sim_solms$PT), 1)` s at trough and
`r round(max(sim_solms$PT), 1)` s at peak, inside the 10-40 s range the paper
quotes for patients on rivaroxaban measured with this reagent.

## Regimen ratios of the covariate-only exposures (Table S3)

Table S3 lists the median covariate-only exposures in the EINSTEIN-DVT/PE
phase III population for 15 mg twice daily and 20 mg once daily. Both regimens
are evaluated over the *same* patients, so their AUC0-24 ratio depends almost
only on the dose-dependent bioavailability and the daily dose -- not on the
undisclosed covariate distribution -- and is a sharp check on the F1 function
of the fixed PK layer.

```{r regimen-ratio}
ev_bid <- make_events(1L, 15, 12, 20, seq(216, 240, by = 0.25), ref_cov)
ev_od <- make_events(1L, 20, 24, 10, seq(216, 240, by = 0.25), ref_cov)

auc_cmax_ctrough <- function(ev) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    ui, ev,
    omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  data.frame(
    auc = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2),
    cmax = max(s$Cc),
    ctrough = s$Cc[s$time == 240]
  )
}
ratio <- auc_cmax_ctrough(ev_bid) / auc_cmax_ctrough(ev_od)

regimen_tbl <- data.frame(
  metric = c("AUC0-24", "Cmax", "Ctrough"),
  table_s3 = c(4082.78 / 2508.44, 235.66 / 221.00, 94.96 / 25.07),
  model = unname(unlist(ratio))
)
regimen_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(table_s3, model), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Ratio 15 mg b.d. / 20 mg o.d." = metric,
    "Table S3 medians" = table_s3,
    "Model, typical patient" = model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# AUC0-24 ratio: 1.5 * F(15 mg) / F(20 mg); within 2% of the published ratio.
stopifnot(abs(ratio$auc / (4082.78 / 2508.44) - 1) < 0.02)
```

The Cmax and Ctrough ratios also depend on the elimination rate, so they are
reported for comparison only; the typical-patient values are within a few
percent of the population medians.

## The PT-adjustment functions reproduce Table 3

Table 2 gives the linear PT-adjustment functions,
`adjustment factor = intercept + slope * PT covariate`. Applying them to the
PT-covariate percentiles of Table 3 must return the adjustment-factor
percentiles printed in the same table (a monotone function maps percentiles
onto percentiles). This checks the transcription of Table 2 used in the
sections below.

```{r table2-table3}
adj_fun <- tibble::tribble(
  ~metric, ~intercept, ~slope,
  "AUC0-24", -0.0147, 1.02,
  "Cmax", 0.34, 0.659,
  "Ctrough", -1.14, 2.27
)

table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~indication, ~row, ~p_min, ~p05, ~p50, ~p95, ~p_max,
  "AF", "PT covariate", 0.55, 0.77, 1.02, 1.56, 3.19,
  "AF", "AUC0-24", 0.55, 0.77, 1.03, 1.58, 3.24,
  "AF", "Cmax", 0.70, 0.85, 1.01, 1.37, 2.44,
  "AF", "Ctrough", 0.10, 0.60, 1.18, 2.41, 6.10,
  "VTE treatment", "PT covariate", 0.58, 0.83, 1.06, 1.39, 2.95,
  "VTE treatment", "AUC0-24", 0.58, 0.84, 1.07, 1.41, 3.00,
  "VTE treatment", "Cmax", 0.72, 0.89, 1.04, 1.26, 2.28,
  "VTE treatment", "Ctrough", 0.18, 0.75, 1.27, 2.02, 5.55,
  "VTE prevention", "PT covariate", 0.71, 0.88, 1.05, 1.41, 2.81,
  "VTE prevention", "AUC0-24", 0.71, 0.89, 1.06, 1.42, 2.86,
  "VTE prevention", "Cmax", 0.81, 0.92, 1.03, 1.27, 2.19,
  "VTE prevention", "Ctrough", 0.47, 0.86, 1.25, 2.05, 5.25
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(p_min:p_max, names_to = "percentile")

pt_cov <- table3 |>
  dplyr::filter(row == "PT covariate") |>
  dplyr::select(indication, percentile, pt = value)

recon <- table3 |>
  dplyr::filter(row != "PT covariate") |>
  dplyr::rename(metric = row, printed = value) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pt_cov, by = c("indication", "percentile")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(adj_fun, by = "metric") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    computed = intercept + slope * pt,
    diff = computed - printed
  )

recon |>
  dplyr::filter(percentile %in% c("p05", "p50", "p95")) |>
  dplyr::select(indication, metric, percentile, printed, computed) |>
  dplyr::mutate(computed = round(computed, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Indication" = indication, "Factor" = metric, "Percentile" = percentile,
    "Table 3" = printed, "Table 2 function" = computed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

# Deterministic: the PT covariate is printed to 0.005, which the Ctrough slope
# of 2.27 amplifies to 0.011, plus 0.005 for rounding of the printed factor.
# All 45 cells must agree within that.
max_dev <- max(abs(recon$diff))
max_dev
stopifnot(nrow(recon) == 45, max_dev < 0.017)
```

All 45 cells agree within `r round(max_dev, 3)`, so Table 3 was generated with
exactly the Table 2 functions and no floor or cap on the adjustment factor.

# Virtual cohort

The exposure comparisons below use the atrial fibrillation indication, the
largest phase III population in the paper (Table S1). Solms 2019 does not
tabulate demographics, so the cohort reproduces the ROCKET AF PK-substudy row
of Willmann 2018a Table 1 -- the same 161 patients who contributed the AF data
to the PK/PT fit: age 65.46 (SD 9.51) years, weight 85.40 (SD 18.60) kg, serum
creatinine 1.09 (SD 0.29) mg/dL, BSA 1.96 (SD 0.22) m^2, 37.9% female.
Creatinine clearance is derived with Cockcroft-Gault rather than drawn, and the
ROCKET AF dose rule is applied (15 mg once daily at CrCL below 50 mL/min,
otherwise 20 mg; Table 1).

Random effects are drawn in base R from the model's own `$omega` and passed as
data columns, so the cohort is identical on every machine; the PT residual
error is likewise drawn in base R.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190704)
n_sub <- 200 # one arm; validation cohorts are capped at 200 per arm

cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  AGE = pmax(18, rnorm(n_sub, 65.46, 9.51)),
  WT = pmax(40, rnorm(n_sub, 85.40, 18.60)),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.379),
  SCR = pmax(0.4, rnorm(n_sub, 1.09, 0.29)),
  BSA = pmax(1.3, rnorm(n_sub, 1.96, 0.22))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    CRCL = (140 - AGE) * WT / (72 * SCR) * ifelse(SEXF == 1, 0.85, 1),
    dose = ifelse(CRCL < 50, 15, 20),
    CONMED_PGP_INH = 0, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_STRONG = 0,
    CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_MOD = 0, CONMED_CYP3A4_INH_WEAK = 0,
    CONMED_CYP3A4_IND = 0, DIS_AF = 1, DIS_ACS = 0, DIS_VTE_P = 0
  )

omega <- ui$omega
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_sub * nrow(omega)), n_sub) %*% chol(omega)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)
eta <- tibble::as_tibble(eta) |> dplyr::mutate(id = cohort$id)

stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(omega), c("etalka", "etalcl", "etalvc", "etalrbase", "etalslope")),
  abs(mean(cohort$CRCL) - 81.76) < 25
)
table(cohort$dose)
```

# Simulation

Ten days of once-daily dosing reach steady state (the typical half-life is
`r round(log(2) * 62.5172 / (6.58214 * 0.84858), 1)` h in AF). The final
dosing interval is observed every 0.25 h.

```{r simulate}
tau <- 24
n_dose <- 10
t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
obs_times <- seq(t_last, t_last + tau, by = 0.25)

events <- cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(\(d, k) {
    make_events(k$id, d$dose, tau, n_dose, obs_times, dplyr::select(d, -dose)) |>
      dplyr::select(-id)
  }) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::relocate(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, dvid) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Covariate-only solve (all etas zero) and individual solve (etas as data
# columns override the zero etas under omega = NA).
sim_cov <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui, events,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
)
sim_ind <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui, dplyr::left_join(events, eta, by = "id"),
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(sim_cov) == n_sub * length(obs_times),
  nrow(sim_ind) == nrow(sim_cov),
  !anyNA(sim_ind$Cc), !anyNA(sim_ind$PT), all(sim_ind$Cc >= 0),
  # the eta columns really were applied: individual CL/F differs from the
  # covariate-only CL/F for (essentially) every subject
  mean(abs(sim_ind$cl / sim_cov$cl - 1) > 1e-6) > 0.99
)

# Observed PT = individual prediction with proportional residual error.
sim_ind$PT_obs <- sim_ind$PT * (1 + rnorm(nrow(sim_ind), 0, 0.114))
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r fig-profiles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state rivaroxaban concentration and prothrombin time over one dosing interval in the atrial fibrillation cohort (median and 5th-95th percentiles, individual predictions). The PT panel corresponds to the steady-state PT profiles that Figure S5a of Solms 2019 shows for the phase III VTE-treatment population."}
sim_ind |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, PT), names_to = "endpoint") |>
  dplyr::mutate(endpoint = dplyr::recode(
    endpoint,
    Cc = "Rivaroxaban (ug/L)", PT = "Prothrombin time (s)"
  )) |>
  dplyr::group_by(endpoint, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = quantile(value, 0.05), med = median(value),
    hi = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig-pkpt, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates the layout of Figure S2 of Solms 2019: time-matched simulated concentrations and observed PT (with residual error), with the typical linear relationship PT = 13.1 + 0.031 Cc in red."}
set.seed(2)
pkpt <- sim_ind |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::slice_sample(n = 4) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

ggplot(pkpt, aes(Cc, PT_obs)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 13.1, slope = 0.031, colour = "red", linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "Rivaroxaban concentration (ug/L)", y = "Prothrombin time (s)") +
  theme_bw()

# Least-squares refit of the simulated PK-PT pairs recovers the typical line
# within the spread the IIV allows (SLOPE CV 38%): a mis-scaled Cc (ng/L vs
# ug/L) or a transposed BASE/SLOPE moves these by orders of magnitude.
fit <- stats::lm(PT_obs ~ Cc, data = pkpt)
coef(fit)
stopifnot(
  abs(coef(fit)[[1]] / 13.1 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(coef(fit)[[2]] / 0.031 - 1) < 0.3
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The covariate-only steady-state exposures (all random effects zero) are the
quantity Table S1 summarises as "Exposure based on covariates" for the AF
population.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_cov |>
  dplyr::mutate(nca_time = time - t_last, treatment = "AF, 20 mg o.d. (15 mg at CrCL < 50)") |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, nca_time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))

nca_dose <- cohort |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, treatment = "AF, 20 mg o.d. (15 mg at CrCL < 50)",
    nca_time = 0, dose
  )

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  as.data.frame(nca_conc), Cc ~ nca_time | treatment + id,
  concu = "ug/L", timeu = "h"
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  as.data.frame(nca_dose), dose ~ nca_time | treatment + id,
  doseu = "mg"
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = tau, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE,
  ctrough = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
stopifnot(
  all(c("cmax", "auclast", "ctrough") %in% nca_tbl$PPTESTCD),
  !anyNA(nca_tbl$PPORRES[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "ctrough")])
)
```

```{r nca-comparison}
reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = "AF, 20 mg o.d. (15 mg at CrCL < 50)",
  auclast = 3312.89, cmax = 252.38, ctrough = 47.23
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_tbl |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "ctrough")),
  reference,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "ug*h/L", cmax = "ug/L", ctrough = "ug/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Median covariate-only steady-state exposure in atrial fibrillation: simulated vs Table S1 'Exposure based on covariates' (N = 7,111). AUC0-24 is PKNCA auclast over the 0-24 h dosing interval.")
attr(cmp, "footnote")

sim_med <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "ctrough")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .by = PPTESTCD)
pct <- with(sim_med, med[match(c("auclast", "cmax", "ctrough"), PPTESTCD)]) /
  c(3312.89, 252.38, 47.23) - 1
round(100 * pct, 1)
# Centre of the distribution only (assertion style for cohorts): a wrong CL/F,
# F1 or unit factor moves these by tens of percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(pct) < 0.2))
```

# The PT covariate approach on simulated phase III data

The paper's preferred approach (Methods; Supplementary Model Code, "R Script
of PT-covariate approach") computes, for each patient, the geometric mean of
observed PT divided by the PT expected from the covariate-only concentration
and the typical PK/PT line. That **PT covariate** is turned into an exposure
adjustment factor with the Table 2 functions. Phase III patients had a median
of two PT samples each (Table 1); here two samples per patient are taken at
random times in the steady-state dosing interval.

```{r pt-covariate}
set.seed(3)
samp <- sim_ind |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, PT_obs) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(sim_cov, id, time, Cc_cov = Cc),
    by = c("id", "time")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::slice_sample(n = 2) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    pt_cov = exp(mean(log(PT_obs / (13.1 + 0.031 * Cc_cov)))),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

auc_ratio <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, auc_cov = PPORRES)
# Individual AUC0-24 by the trapezoidal rule on the same 0.25 h grid.
auc_ind <- sim_ind |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    auc_ind = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ptc <- samp |>
  dplyr::left_join(auc_ratio, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(auc_ind, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    true_ratio = auc_ind / auc_cov,
    adj_auc = -0.0147 + 1.02 * pt_cov
  )

pt_q <- quantile(ptc$pt_cov, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
data.frame(
  percentile = c("5th", "Median", "95th"),
  table3 = c(0.77, 1.02, 1.56),
  simulated = round(unname(pt_q), 2)
) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Percentile" = percentile, "Table 3, AF" = table3,
    "Simulated" = simulated
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PT covariate in atrial fibrillation: simulated vs Table 3.")

r2 <- stats::cor(ptc$adj_auc, ptc$true_ratio)^2
r2
# Centre of the PT covariate sits near 1 (the expected PT matches the observed
# PT for a typical patient), and the PT covariate carries real information on
# the unexplained AUC variability (positive correlation, as in Figure 3).
stopifnot(
  abs(median(ptc$pt_cov) - 1.02) < 0.1,
  stats::cor(ptc$adj_auc, ptc$true_ratio) > 0.2
)
```

```{r fig-ptcov, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Analogue of Figure 3 of Solms 2019 (PT covariate approach): PT-adjusted (predicted) vs true prediction-corrected AUC0-24 in the simulated AF cohort; the dashed line is identity."}
ggplot(ptc, aes(true_ratio, adj_auc)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "True prediction-corrected AUC0-24",
    y = "PT-adjusted prediction-corrected AUC0-24"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

As in the paper, the PT-adjusted predictions are correlated with the true
individual exposures but compressed towards 1: PT cannot replace a PK sample,
and the adjusted distribution is narrower than the true one.

The simulated PT covariate is centred where Table 3 puts it, and its lower
tail matches, but its upper tail is shorter (95th percentile
`r round(pt_q[[3]], 2)` vs 1.56). The simulation contains only the variability
the PK/PT model describes -- PK IIV, BASE and SLOPE IIV, and an 11.4%
residual error -- at exactly steady state. The phase III PT data also carry
departures the model does not describe: non-adherence, varying time on
treatment, imputed covariates and unrecorded comedication. These widen the
observed ratio distribution, mostly upwards (the maximum PT covariate in
Table 3 is 3.19). Only the centre is asserted.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PK residual error.** The PK `$SIGMA` of the popPK/PT control stream has no
  FIX flag, so it was re-estimated together with the PT data, but its final
  value is not reported. The control-stream value 0.203389 (the Willmann 2018a
  final variance; SD 0.450555) is used.
* **IIV on BASE.** The Results print a variance of 0.006 with
  "SD = 0.0757, CV = 7.76%". The CV is consistent with the variance
  (log(1 + 0.0776^2) = 0.0060); the SD is not (0.0757^2 = 0.0057). The printed
  variance 0.006 is used.
* **Integer subject counts.** Table 1 sums to 1,779 patients with valid PK and
  PT samples; the Results text gives 831 + 788 + 161 = 1,780.
* **Comedication and indication.** The PK/PT data contain no ACS patients; the
  ACS factor is carried from the fixed PK layer for completeness.
* **Cohort.** Solms 2019 does not tabulate the demographics of the PK-PT data
  set or of the phase III populations, so the AF cohort follows the ROCKET AF
  row of Willmann 2018a Table 1 with no comedication. Table S1 summarises
  7,111 ROCKET AF patients, of whom only the 161 PK-substudy patients share
  these demographics, so the comparison against Table S1 is of the centre of
  the distribution only.
* **PT sampling times.** The timing of phase III PT samples relative to dose is
  not reported; two random times within the steady-state dosing interval are
  assumed (the paper excludes PT measured more than 30 h after a dose).
* **PT-adjustment functions.** Table 2 is a post-hoc regression, not part of
  the simulation model, and is applied outside `model()`. The paper's
  alternative "eta approach" (post hoc PK estimates from PT alone, using the
  same PK/PT model with the PT IIV set to zero and an assumed 45% PT residual
  error) is not packaged; it is an estimation recipe rather than a different
  model.
